prerequisites.text: Hold a valid Arizona hunting license (resident general hunting or combination; nonresident combination) on the day you apply and through the deadline, or buy one with the application. This applies to point-only applications too.
prerequisites.quote: An applicant must have possession of a valid license at the time of entry and the deadline of the application period per R12-4-104.

prerequisites.text: Apply online with an AZGFD portal account; results are posted only in the portal. Keep the card on file current, or the application is not drawn.
prerequisites.quote: AZGFD portal accounts now are the sole source for finding out draw results and viewing bonus points.

prerequisites.text: Hunter education is required only for youth under 14 to hunt big game. No one under 10 may hunt big game, and point-only applicants must be 10 by the deadline.
prerequisites.quote: Hunter Education is only required for youth under the age of 14 to hunt big game in Arizona.

notes: Arizona has three big-game draws: pronghorn/elk (deadline in February), fall deer/bighorn sheep/bison (June), and spring (October; for big game in scope, only spring bison). The spring 2027 draw has closed (Oct. 6, 2026) and its results are posted; draw.azgfd.com says to check back in January for the 2027 elk/pronghorn draw. The 2027 pronghorn/elk and fall 2027 deer/sheep booklets are not published yet, so those rows show 2026 dates, marked last_year. Exact opening dates are not given: the booklets say only 'early to mid-January', 'early to mid-May' and 'early to mid-September'. Exact draw-results dates are not printed either. The booklets give only 'tags mailed out by' dates: April 1, 2026 (elk/pronghorn), July 24, 2026 (fall) and Nov. 25, 2026 (spring 2027). Bonus-point-only applications are made in the same draw, using the bonus point hunt number. Fees come from the 2027 spring booklet and match the 2026–27 booklet that says it is valid for 2026 hunts. Permit-tag prices include the application fee. AZ has no moose or mountain goat hunts. Youth-only hunt prices in the PDF table come out as '$637'/'$657' (elk) and '$387'/'$407' (deer), most likely $63/$65 and $38/$40 followed by footnote 7. Because that reading is uncertain, they are not recorded. azgfd.com returns a Cloudflare challenge to automated requests, so the agency's S3-hosted PDFs were used; the howToUrl page could not be fetched.
